top_selection.comment: A package is 'top' if it falls within the top X% of cumulative download mass in its ecosystem

fetch_ttl_days.comment: Cache TTL in days for every fetcher, keyed by its module path under src/ (a module with two independent caches gets a dotted suffix). A fetcher re-fetches only when its cached data is older than this, so a warm checkout runs --offline for a year without touching the network. --refresh overrides any of them. Every fetcher MUST have a key here: params.fetch_ttl_days() raises on an unknown one, so a new fetcher cannot silently default. Back-off windows are not cache TTLs and live in fetch_retry_days.

fetch_retry_days.comment: Back-off windows, NOT cache TTLs. These govern how soon a FAILED or empty result is retried, so they stay short — stretching them to a year would leave a transient failure unretried for a year.

downloads_score.comment: downloads_score = debian_weight*debian_avg + homebrew_weight*homebrew_avg. Default ratio 1.39:1 is inverse of ecosystem totals (debian ~181.9M vs homebrew ~252.8M annual installs) so a 'typical' package from either ecosystem contributes equally.

value_classes.comment: Cumulative PageRank share intervals [lo, hi] per class (upper bound inclusive). Class A (<=75%) is also the risk-pipeline input scope; see risk_input.value_classes.

risk_input.comment: Risk pipeline runs on valid class-A repos (value/value.csv class == 'A'). Kept as the documented risk scope; load_top_repos reads top_repos below.

top_repos.comment: load_top_repos scope — a value.csv row is a 'top repo' iff platform in platforms AND class in classes AND git_valid==True. GitHub + GitLab: the risk builders rank each percentile-based dimension over the full top-repo population (github + gitlab together — platform does not matter), so GitLab repos rank in alongside GitHub. classes must match risk_input.value_classes.

value_score.comment: value.csv `score`, 0-100: a pro-rata blend of up to four components — openssf_crit (weight criticality_weight; OpenSSF criticality score 0-1, scaled *100), eco_crit (weight eco_crit_weight; ecosyste.ms critical flag, stored 0/100), top_eco_pct (weight centrality_weight; the repo's PageRank percentile in its top ecosystem, already 0-100), and pr_score (weight pr_score_weight; cross-ecosystem dependency-mass score, already 0-100). Only PRESENT (non-blank) components are summed, then renormalized by their weight total, so a repo missing some still scores on the same 0-100 scale. A row needs at least min_components present or `score` stays blank. Full weights (0.6/0.2/0.1/0.1) sum to 1 and are criticality-dominant so a foundational-but-quiet micro-dep can't outrank a genuinely critical project; the two PageRank-family factors (position vs mass) share the former 0.2 centrality weight. openssf_crit is GitHub-only; eco_crit covers GitHub and GitLab; top_eco_pct + pr_score cover every repo with a PageRank signal, so valid GitLab class-A repos score even when both crits are unknown.

concentration.comment: window_years: '_5y' window length in complete years anchored to max(years) (the last complete year); '_full' = all commits through max(years). bus_factor_threshold: commit-share that defines the bus factor (0.5 = the fewest contributors covering 50% of commits). concentration.csv column names stay year-agnostic (_5y / _full); the year boundary lives here, not in the schema.
